name: onion_service
title: D. Rendezvous vs Tor onion service
summary: A stable .onion address is a stable network identifier: continuity by design. HsDirs see descriptor publication times; introduction points and guards allow timing correlation on live circuits; interaction requires both parties online.

assumptions.join_kinds: ROOT_IDENTITY | RELATIONSHIP_IDENTITY | PAIRWISE_KEY | NETWORK_IDENTIFIER | SOURCE_ENDPOINT | DEST_ENDPOINT | TRANSACTION_ID | OBLIGATION_ID | CONTEXT_ID | RELATIONSHIP_LINK | ASSET | DENOMINATION | AMOUNT | TIME | CONTENT | CONTENT_SIZE | NETWORK_LOCATION | SESSION_IDENTIFIER

provenance: Authors' model of Tor onion-service rendezvous disclosure (S11.D), 2026-09-03.
omitted: Guard rotation and its (slow) continuity improvement.
Global passive observers (out of threat model, S0); Tor's own live-circuit timing correlation is noted in the summary.
not_better_when: You need location protection: Tor protects location, Molt protects continuity. Composed, each covers the other's gap.
joins_remaining_notes: Relays see the poller's network location unless a Tor adapter is on the route.
The root is public because Pubky wants it to be; discovery is already decentralized via PKARR.
No live-circuit timing: messages sit in a queue (asynchronous store-and-forward).
